sources.entry: TurboFieldfare - Native ChatGPT-like Mac app running Google’s Gemma AI (26B-A4B MoE) privately on your device, even on low-end 8 GB M-series Macs. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/drumih/turbo-fieldfare) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: TurboFieldfare is a native Swift and Metal runtime and Mac app that runs the instruction-tuned Gemma 4 26B-A4B model on Apple Silicon Macs by streaming expert weights from SSD, keeping memory use to about 2 GB.
summary.what_it_does: TurboFieldfare runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B without loading the full 14.3 GB model into memory. It keeps the shared core and FP16 KV cache resident and streams only the routed experts needed for each token from SSD, with a 16-slot LFU expert cache. The project includes a streaming installer that downloads a pinned Hugging Face checkpoint and repacks it into its own .gturbo format while validating hashes. It ships a SwiftUI/AppKit Mac app with saved local chat history, a CLI for instruction chat and raw completion, and an experimental loopback OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions server with streaming and function tool declarations. Optional image input is available through a separately installed 1.1 GB vision pack on M2 or newer Macs. The README states the model is not wrapped around MLX or llama.cpp.
use_cases: run a 26B language model on an 8 GB Mac
private offline chat with a local model
benchmark local LLM decode speed on Apple Silicon
serve a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint for coding tools
ask questions about a photo with a local model on a Mac
study Metal kernel and MoE expert streaming design
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd turbo-fieldfare
In the app, choose Download Model (about 15 GB) and then Load Model
swift build -c release --product TurboFieldfareServer, then run .build/release/TurboFieldfareServer --model scratch/gemma4.gturbo
Scripts/test.sh runs the public test suite serially
notable: Streams routed MoE experts from SSD with a bounded expert cache, so a 26B model fits in roughly 2 GB of RAM
Streaming installer repacks remote Hugging Face byte ranges directly into .gturbo without a full local checkpoint
Model-specific engine written in Swift and Metal rather than a wrapper around MLX or llama.cpp
Includes a native Mac app, CLI, and loopback OpenAI-compatible server sharing one model directory
Optional vision tower companion pack for image input, with the app built by a script using ad-hoc signing
caveats: Requires an arm64 Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26 with Metal 4 and Swift 6.2+; older macOS and Metal are not supported
Image input requires an M2 or newer Mac; M1 is text-only
Server is experimental, has no remote authentication or TLS, and must stay on loopback; audio and video are not supported
Initial install transfers about 15 GB and needs about 14.3 GB free storage; measured decode is about 5.5–6.8 tok/s on an 8 GB M2 Air and 35–39 tok/s on a 24 GB M5 Pro
